title: Build a SoC and run a program on it
nav_title: Build a SoC and run a program
lede: Copy the supplied SoC manifest, choose its core, run a C program on it in simulation, then build it for a Nexys Video and upload the program over UART.
prerequisites: The tools from [Install tools and run a simulation](#/guides/getting-started#1-install-the-tools).
For the board stages: a Nexys Video, and Vivado with Artix-7 support.
outcome: Your own SoC manifest and system manifest, and a C program that runs on them in simulation and on the board.

stages.title: Install the tools
stages.text: Install the simulator, Make and the RISC-V compiler, and set the toolchain prefix.

stages.title: Copy the SoC manifest
stages.text: Copy the supplied SoC manifest to `local/soc.toml`. This one file describes your hardware: the core, the memory sizes and the peripherals. Check it, then run the RAM test.

stages.title: Choose the core, its caches and its options
stages.text: A tile manifest, `local/tile.toml`, names the core and its two caches; changing the core or a cache is one line there. The core manifest requests its compiler ISA and microarchitecture settings; Base uses its ISA string to include or remove hardware multiply and divide. Read how the supplied cores differ, then make the edits.

guide.section: 3. Add or remove integer multiply and divide

stages.title: Run a C program in simulation
stages.text: Build the blink program with Make and run it on your SoC in the simulator, before any board is involved.

stages.title: Connect clocks, UART and LEDs
stages.text: Create `local/system.toml`. It names your SoC manifest, sets the clock frequencies and says which board pins carry the UART and the LEDs.

stages.title: Build and program the board
stages.text: Build the bitstream from your system manifest and program the FPGA. If timing fails, lower the CPU clock and build again.

guide.section: 2. Handle a clock or timing failure

stages.title: Upload the program
stages.text: Build the program for the board and send it to the ROM loader over UART. Later program changes need only a rebuild and an upload.
